title: Find the driver who recorded the fastest lap time during the second qualify
question: Find the driver who recorded the fastest lap time during the second qualifying session (Q2) at the most recent British Grand Prix held at Silverstone Circuit, and return their full name along with the race date.

prediction.sql:
SELECT d."XCL_038", d."XCL_039", r."XCL_070"
FROM qualifying q
JOIN races r ON r."XCL_065" = q."XCL_057"
JOIN circuits c ON c."XCL_001" = r."XCL_068"
JOIN drivers d ON d."XCL_034" = q."XCL_058"
WHERE r."XCL_069" = 'British Grand Prix'
  AND c."XCL_003" = 'Silverstone Circuit'
  AND q."XCL_063" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY r."XCL_066" DESC, r."XCL_070" DESC, q."XCL_063" ASC
LIMIT 1

roles.description: Lap time recorded in the first qualifying session (Q1). This is the most frequently populated time column, serving as the baseline for all qualifying entries.
Lap time recorded in the second qualifying session (Q2). This column is populated only for drivers who advanced from Q1, exhibiting a strict subset relationship with Q1 times.
Lap time recorded in the third qualifying session (Q3). This column is populated only for drivers who advanced from Q2, exhibiting a strict subset relationship with Q2 times.

structural_constraints.description: Participation in the second qualifying session (Q2) implies participation in the first qualifying session (Q1). The data confirms this: every row with a Q2 time has a Q1 time, but many rows with a Q1 time do not have a Q2 time.

Participation in the third qualifying session (Q3) implies participation in the second qualifying session (Q2). The data confirms this: every row with a Q3 time has a Q2 time, but many rows with a Q2 time do not have a Q3 time.

The fastest Q2 lap is selected by ordering qualifying.XCL_063 ASC; observed Q2 values are M:SS.mmm lap-time strings, so lexical ascending order corresponds to shorter duration for the relevant value range.
The join grain is one qualifying row per driver per race, so no duplicate driver rows are introduced by the drivers, races, or circuits joins.
The returned columns are drivers.XCL_038, drivers.XCL_039, and races.XCL_070, matching the requested full name and race date without concatenation.

base_solution_anchor.base_sql:
SELECT d."XCL_038", d."XCL_039", r."XCL_070"
FROM qualifying q
JOIN drivers d ON d."XCL_034" = q."XCL_058"
JOIN races r ON r."XCL_065" = q."XCL_057"
JOIN circuits c ON c."XCL_001" = r."XCL_068"
WHERE r."XCL_069" = 'British Grand Prix'
  AND c."XCL_003" = 'Silverstone Circuit'
  AND q."XCL_061" = 2
ORDER BY r."XCL_066" DESC, q."XCL_062" ASC
LIMIT 1

auxiliary_raw_evidence_draft.base_sql:
SELECT 
    d.XCL_037 || ' ' || d.XCL_038 AS full_name,
    r.XCL_070 AS race_date
FROM qualifying q
JOIN races r ON q.XCL_057 = r.XCL_065
JOIN circuits c ON r.XCL_068 = c.XCL_001
JOIN drivers d ON q.XCL_058 = d.XCL_034
WHERE c.XCL_003 = 'Silverstone Circuit'
  AND r.XCL_069 = 'British Grand Prix'
  AND q.XCL_060 = 2
ORDER BY r.XCL_070 DESC, q.XCL_062 ASC
LIMIT 1
